A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pyramidal flow matching work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench and EvalCrafter evaluations, a human preference study, generation examples, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds MSR-VTT convergence results, image examples, and a synthetic noise-coupling experiment.

M1.justification: The spatial and temporal pyramids, coupled endpoint sampling, flow-matching objective, corrective renoising, causal attention, and model architecture remain unchanged. Appendix C.4 tests the existing coupling procedure rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: v2 adds MSR-VTT evaluation in Figure 12b and synthetic point-to-uniform-distribution scenarios in Appendix C.4. Training corpora and existing benchmarks remain unchanged. Text-to-image generation was already evaluated in v1, so Figure 12a adds examples rather than a new task.

E2.justification: The VBench comparisons replace Open-Sora Plan v1.1 with v1.3 in Table 1 and the detailed appendix table. The user study still uses v1.1. Appendix C.4 also introduces random coupling as a comparator; the other established comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce FVD measured across training iterations and a two-stage toy setup with one or three data points. Existing training schedules, model sizes, benchmark generation settings, and user-study procedures remain unchanged; the new FVD evaluation receives little protocol detail.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a controlled comparison testing whether endpoint coupling produces straighter trajectories. Figure 12b adds quantitative video convergence evidence beyond v1's qualitative temporal-pyramid comparison in Figure 8. Existing spatial, temporal, renoising, and causal-attention ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v2 adds no uncertainty estimates. The user-study counts remain 50 prompts, more than 20 participants, and 1,411 valid preferences.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Open-Sora Plan v1.1 results with v1.3 results, including total score 78.00 versus 77.23; this compares different baseline versions. Figures 12–13 add image outputs, lower FVD than full-sequence diffusion across the plotted iterations, and straighter coupled trajectories. The proposed model's existing benchmark scores and user-preference results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction and Appendix A derivation are retained. v2 explicitly writes conditioning on x1 where v1 already describes conditional distributions, and Table 3 summarizes existing notation. The coupling experiment and intuitive explanation add no theorem, proof, or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified spatial and temporal pyramidal flow matching, efficient training, competitive video quality, and 5–10-second generation at 768p and 24 FPS within 20.7k A100 GPU hours. New appendix evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 newly explains coupling through more organized trajectories with fewer intersections, expanding v1's brief straightness motivation. Appendix D adds real-time inference efficiency as an open problem. Existing limitations concerning interpolation, subject consistency, captions, and scene transitions remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code and model release; v2 reports them as open-sourced and adds a reproducibility statement directing readers to the experimental settings. Architecture, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds f-DM and Dimensionality-varying diffusion process to the multistage generation discussion. v2 also adds references for MSR-VTT and fast causal video generators. The central research positioning remains unchanged; the Show-1 bibliographic revision refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited introduction and conclusion edits, clarifies conditional notation, adds Appendix C.4 and a reproducibility statement, and revises affiliations, acknowledgments, and publication headers. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds notation Table 3, the image/FVD panels in Figure 12, and coupling plots in Figure 13. Existing appendix tables and figures reflow, while v1's video galleries in Figures 12–13 become Figures 14–15 with the same images. The main visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplements v1's qualitative temporal ablation with quantitative MSR-VTT convergence evidence and provides a useful experiment and explanation for noise coupling. The notation guide and reported code/model release also improve usability. These are limited gains: the new evaluations have sparse protocol detail and no uncertainty estimates, while the core method and headline results remain unchanged.
